utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy -- Madam Court Deputy. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, any re-examination, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Re-examined by Mr. Weiner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Mehanovic.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you were asked by Defence counsel about the visit of Sefer Halilovic, Zuka Alispago, and Vehbija Karic to Grabovica on September 9th. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall -- prior to testifying yesterday, do you recall ever being asked questions or ever telling other people during questions about that visit?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you were also questioned, questions on several occasions, concerning your interview with the cantonal court on the 12th of January, 1999. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall - and I'm reading from page 3 in the English- do you recall telling the cantonal court: "During the time we spent in Grabovica, some of the members of the Supreme Command came for a visit, among them Vehbija Karic, Zuka, and Sefer." Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say said "Sefer"" or used the name "Sefer," who were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall giving a statement to OTP investigator Nikolai Mikhailov on the 11th of November, 1999? Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on page 4 in the English, do you recall saying: "When Vehbija uttered those words, three commanders were present too, including Sefer Halilovic and Zuka"? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said here, Vehbija Karic was there, Zuka, and Mr. Halilovic, of the senior officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also recall in the year 2004 on the 20th of October giving a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor investigator Bernard Brun and attorney Manoj Sachdeva and do you recall saying on page 2, which would be paragraph 11 in the English version --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd object to this. That statement wasn't cross-examined on. The other ones were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Unless -- unless you establish some connections with the cross-examination, this question is not allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: However, Your Honour, yesterday he questioned the witness and said, "You" -- and he said, "You never said anything about Sefer Halilovic being at this location prior," I think, "to 1999. " Although this is in 2004, it shows that he made the statement, number one, to at least one investigator -- this is the third investigator he's made the statement to. And in addition, he also questioned him about some sort of recent conspiracy with Mr. -- with another witness, since we're not in closed session, and I want to also show that prior to yesterday or prior to their recent meeting, he also gave that same information, as he had given since 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But the form of your question is not proper. You may put it another way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall speaking with investigator Bernard Brun of the Office of the Prosecutor in the year 2000?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, the objection remains the same. He wasn't questioned about this statement. And if my friend persists with it, I'll respond to the justification that he gave a minute ago. Your Honour, what was put to the witness in substance was that he's discussed the evidence, he's associated with the other people that were raised in closed session yesterday. The news about the recent discussion, as Your Honours saw, was very recent news and he was cross-examined about that before that actually came out, as you'll recall. So it's not being put that there was a conspiracy invented only the other night. That's not the case. So that this is not evidence that rebuts that in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, you may quote what the Defence counsel said in his cross-examination and then ask this witness to say whether it's true or not and later on you could follow up your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll go into that in a few moments, Your Honour. Sir, let us move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, sir,-- actually, let us continue with the situation that you discussed where Sefer Halilovic, Zuka Alispago, Vehbija Karic visited Grabovica. Do you recall being asked by Defence counsel about an older Croat man who was standing on the balcony while those commanders were visiting?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he asked you if they asked that Croat man to leave or go inside the house.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did they ask?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's -- and do you recall counsel saying, "Did they ask that old man to go inside the house or leave"? Do you recall that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know if it was like that. As far as I can remember, I was asked whether anybody would speak in front of the enemy side, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct. Now, when you were asked, you -- the counsel asked you would anyone discuss military operations in front of -- I'll actually give you the exact quote -- discuss an upcoming operation in front of the -- a civilian from the opposite side. Sir, were any details of the military operation discussed by Sefer Halilovic, Zuka Alispago, or Vehbija Karic in that old man's presence?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any strategies of that operation mentioned in that man's presence?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Sefer Halilovic, Zuka Alispago, or Vehbija Karic display any maps of the operation in that old man's presence?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so, but I cannot remember specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we're talking about whether it would be odd for senior commanders to address troops about operations in the presence of civilians tied to the other side, and you were asked on how many occasions you were aware that that occurred. Let me ask you this, sir: On how many occasions have you noticed a senior commander discuss plans of an upcoming operation with a member of the press being present?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On how many occasions have you noticed any senior commander issue orders on upcoming operations in the presence of a member of the press?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, on how many occasions have you noticed senior commanders displaying maps of upcoming operations to members of the press?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's get back to the earlier issue. Yesterday you were asked two questions: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First, what is your answer to both of those questions?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it's just a silly thing to say. I have no response to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just raise a matter here. I'm not sure what the status of the -- the projected alleged desire of a particular person for protective measures is, but if it's being persisted with, then at least perhaps the Prosecutor ought to go through the form of going to private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think, you know, the purpose of the protective measures is a measure not to disclose the status of that person who would be a witness in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that if the -- the request was raised by the Prosecution yesterday, and if they believe there's no problem at all, we'll not take care of it. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could the name be redacted, Your Honour. My -- my fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, if you request it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall giving a statement -- you recalled giving these other statements where you talked about Sefer Halilovic, Zuka Alispago, and Vehbija Karic visiting Grabovica. Do you recall giving a statement last year to investigator Bernard Brun and attorney Manoj Sachdeva on the 20th of October, 2004?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we seem to be back to the same position we were. And I'd object to references to that unless it arises out of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But the witness has answered the question. We'll let it go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall saying to the investigator and the attorney, "After Halilovic" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it depends on the contents of the question. Let him finish the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually, you start in paragraph 10: "Karic did not ask such things. After Halilovic and Zuka asked such questions, the soldiers started to complain about the bad food and accommodations." Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, now I do object to it for the reasons I've already indicated and nothing new has been led to justify that being put. The objection remains.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if this matter was not raised in cross-examination, I believe that in the redirect the question is not allowed, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, yesterday you testified as to your disagreements with information contained in certain statements. You said your statement to the MUP, the one to the cantonal court, the one to Nikolai Mikhailov. Do you recall that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, do you recall meeting or being interviewed by investigator Bernard Brun in the year 2004?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall at that time making some corrections to the various statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Once again, I object. This wasn't cross-examined upon, and it's just an attempt to get in what the Prosecution might hope to lead as a prior consistent statement. That in itself is not permitted. In the circumstance of this case, it would be completely irrelevant. I want to point out something else to the Court, if I might, arising out of this: At the start of this re-examination by Mr. Weiner -- Mr. Weiner, I'm sorry, what occurred was that Mr. Weiner himself took the witness to specific parts of those very statements and asked him to agree, which he did. And you'll recall that was the very first questions he asked. Now, the Prosecutor simply can't be heard to rely on those statements and what was said in them at the start of re-examination and then at the end of it or at whatever point we are at now to seek to impugn them in order to buttress the position taken by the witness yesterday. You can't ride two horses, especially when they're going in different directions. And I object to this current line of questioning on that basis as well as the first one that I raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. But as for this specific question, I believe that it's related to the answer the witness gave yesterday in answering your questions, so that particular question is allowed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The cites are pages 41 and 95 to the disagreements with the various statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall making some corrections as to the Nikolai Mikhailov statement when you spoke with investigator Bernard Brun?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, let us look at that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I object before that question goes any further. There's just no basis for it. This statement wasn't raised in cross-examination at all. The witness took a particular position when cross-examined. If there's something about that that needs to be clarified, then let it be clarified. I won't object. But going to this statement is just plainly wrong. I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Weiner. Yes, you want to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. On two occasions yesterday the witness made remarks about problems he had with regard to that particular statement. What I want to bring him through and talk -- and bring him through the statement and show him that -- or have him explain that although he has differences as to the vernacular, there is no difference as to the facts, other than one -- one statement -- one particular statement in there. There is no difference as to the facts in that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether that statement was mentioned or not yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you point it out in a specific line --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Page 41, Your Honour. "And the event I'm putting to you is that you didn't sign something unless you knew it's true; is that correct?" That's starting on page -- line 16. "What I say, I expect them to also note down. But it happened that the investigator Nikolai, there is 90 per cent of untruths there. I don't speak in that way, but it's recorded in that statement. There's at least 90 per cent of untruths in that statement." And then he says: "I'm not asking about Nikolai right now." And then they get back to that at another time. And I just want to use that information that there is a consistency in that statement. And if you looked at it, there is no significant gap or problem in that. Although there's a difference of vernacular, the statement -- the information contained therein is true or valid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, first, there's two major problems with what's being submitted there. The first thing is -- is the statement that he now wants to take the witness to, the 2004 statement, is just plainly not referred to at that passage at all. What we're talking about there is a completely different statement. Your Honour will see from -- I don't know if Your Honour has in front of you that transcript of page 41, but what you can see -- and I'd ask the Court just to take the moment to look at it because what's being put here is just -- not deliberately, I'm sure, but it's just plainly misleading. He was being asked questions about a statement to the MUP, the police, the civilian police. That's what the questioning was about. The witness then of his own motion decided to mention the statement to a man he described as Nikolai. And counsel then put to him that we weren't talking about that statement; we're talking about the -- the statement to the police. And we went back on to that statement. But in any event, the statement to which this witness referred is the Nikolai statement, the -- the earlier statement, not the one that Mr. Weiner is now trying to get before the Court. It had nothing whatsoever to do with that. Perhaps Mr. Weiner would take you to the next page he says is of importance, but I'd submit that one there not only doesn't justify the question but what you were told then was just, well, unintentionally misleading. Perhaps the next page will do better.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour the issue was raised -- the issue was raised twice with regard to Nikolai. Once the witness mentioned it and once he was questioned about it. And since the issue is an open issue and since there is an issue as to statements, I think we should be allowed to state at least that he agrees to the information in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Well, I believe that -- I believe that the -- the name "Nikolai" was mentioned yesterday. There's no problem about that. But I am not sure whether that is the 2004 statement or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, that's the 1999 statement. The 2004 statement is the Bernard Brun and Manoj Sachdeva statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But if the 2004 statement was not mentioned at all, what's the reason for you to use it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I just use that as an opening question and got right off of that that, he did in fact make corrections to the other statements in the 2004 statement. And then I was going to finish off with the Nikolai statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So it was just one brief -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think this witness has answered this question already. So your point has been made, that is, the witness made the corrections in the 2004 statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But I'd also like to take him through the 1999 statement and have him agree to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So come to the -- the Nikolai statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The other reference is page 96, where they discuss the Nikolai statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir, I would like to show you a copy of your 1999 statement. It's only a few pages long. Sir, if you look at the first paragraph, it concerns background information. Do you have any disagreement with that information?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I would object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: He wasn't cross-examined on the first paragraph. Now, if my learned friend wants to do this -- this exercise, he's got to stay strictly within the rules and stay relevant to the cross-examination. He can take him to passages, if he can find any, to which this witness was taken by me and he can be asked to explain what he said, why he said it, if there's anything misleading about it. Of course he would be entitled to say it. He's not entitled to start at the start and go to the end, because I didn't do that in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at my hands, I don't have that statement. But as the first question, I believe that the Prosecution is going to familiarise the witness with that statement. So first he will ask a question concerning of the first line. And later on I believe that Mr. Weiner will concentrate on the question you asked yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If -- if it's confined to that one introductory question, I withdraw the objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just look at the first four paragraphs which concern you. Do you agree to that information? Isn't that correct as to who you are and where you served in?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that again. What it's attempting now to do is to get him to adopt the truth of statement which I didn't cross-examine him about. Now, Your Honour -- Your Honour's point, with respect, was correct that to familiarise him with the statement he's looking at is legitimate. For him to look at and it say, "Well, yes, this is the statement we're talking about," of course he's entitled told do that. But to try to get him now to adopt as true certain parts of it is going way outside of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Weiner, you may ask a question whether the witness recognises this statement, whether he made this statement or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, first, do you recognise the statement? Is that yours?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can recognise it, but there are many things in it that are not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that -- in what language was that statement taken?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was speaking Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were you speaking with?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was this Nikolai and an interpreter. It's -- the name of the interpreter is given here as Peter Hewitt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were interviewed, who asked the questions? Was it Nikolai or the interpreter or both?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nikolai.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what language did he speak to you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometimes he would speak our language but not that well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was my next question: What was the quality of his speech in Bosnian?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Poor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall telling him on page 3 that Sefer Halilovic, Zuka Alispago, and Vehbija Karic visited soldiers in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, if there are passages on which I cross-examined directly, then the Prosecutor is entitled to identify them. He should do so by nominating that there was cross-examination on that point. And the proper form of question, as Your Honour has seen a hundred times, as -- more than I have, I'm sure, at this Tribunal and all events, is to say, "You were asked questions in these terms," and proceed on from there. And then that would be proper for Mr. Weiner to do that, to clear up anything misleading I may have put or that I may have upset the witness intentionally or unintentionally, but not to ask general questions like this. This really sounds like evidence in chief, frankly, at the moment, and I object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I missed your decision on that, on his objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I mean that, you know, you have to ask a question first, saying that "Yesterday you were asked a question," the question is as follows --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm trying to move it along.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, sir, you were asked about the meeting where Sefer Halilovic, Zuka Alispago, and Vehbija Karic met with the soldiers at Grabovica. Do you see that in -- is that information contained in that report that you gave to the OTP investigator Mr. Mihajlovic [sic].

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mihajlovic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mihajlovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, I believe that you have to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that information contained in the report?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mentioned a person named Mihajlovic. I never gave a statement to a person with such a name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the Nikolai statement in 1999 that you have in front of you. Is that information there about the three commanders coming and visiting in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you were questioned about arriving at Zuka's base in Donja Jablanica and Zuka's soldiers escorting you to Grabovica and eventually bringing you to a vacant house. Is that information contained in that report?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I object again. This is the same thing that my learned friend has been trying to do since the beginning. He's trying to get the witness to adopt things that are in the statement. What he has to do -- in order to take the witness to this statement in redirect, what he needs to do is say, "You were cross-examined about a part of this statement," and then if there's something about -- something uncertain or something that needs to be cleared up, well, then that can be put to him. But to simply ask him -- to put to him, "You were questioned about a large topic in the case. Does it now appear in this document," is not a proper part of redirect. Because what's in here is only at issue so far as it was raised in cross-examination. And as I've said, I don't object to him taking him to specific parts of this that were put in cross-examination if my friend identifies them, but not the general questions like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that in the redirect examinations, all the questions should be within the scope of the questions put in the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. However --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And -- and we don't have to go into that statement paragraph by paragraph. Yesterday the witness claimed that some of the contents in that statement is not accurate. You may find certain places to ask this witness for the explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, all I'm trying to do is in -- first in redirect examination, you are allowed to further explain, to get a witness to confirm, to get a witness to change a false impression if one is left. And it is my intention not to have him adopt the statement; however, to basically rectify what I believe to be a false impression that was left from yesterday's testimony. And that's all I'm trying to do, to show that the major topics that he spoke about yesterday are all contained in that statement. Spending approximately five minutes. And that he agrees with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, whether his statement is contained in that statement or not is not important. The most important thing is his testimony now in the courtroom. That's the most important evidence before this Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The statements that you gave to Nikolai in 1999, are your words all contained in quotations within that statement?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again there is a lot of untruth here. There are many things that I didn't say in the statement. There are certain words, as I said yesterday, that do not form part of my vocabulary. I don't even know how to pronounce them, and they are written here. It says, for instance, here that I became commander of an assault unit. That is not true. Malicev [phoen] was the commander of the assault unit. There are quite a few such things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, now, while you gave that statement -- once again, I'm sorry, let's take it a step back. Is your statement, that statement in front of you, is that all in quotations or is that the language that Nikolai used after interviewing you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I object to that. I haven't objected to the questions about -- the last series of questions, but the last part of that question there seemed to be -- well, frankly, it's flatly leading and suggests an answer to him, and it just raises another issue which I'll -- I'll raise at the end of redirect. But I do object to it. But there's a -- it's an objection of form, I think, rather than content, I must say, that if the question concerns what the witness has said 17 or 18 times already, that there's misrepresentations of what he said there, well, I don't object to him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: -- asking that, if that's what the question is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, but this question is a general question, you know, concerning of the form of the statement, and the witness claimed that, you know, something is not true in that statement. So I believe that the Prosecution is entitled to clarify this matter with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the form of that statement in front of you, is that in a family room of quotations from you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think this was written the way it was easier for them, because there are many words there that I do not tend to use. Maybe they wrote it up the way they found easier for them. In any case, I find here a lot of things that I certainly didn't say, this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I raise a matter before any questions that may happen to come from the Bench in relation to that. There's now been an attack made both by the witness and through questioning by my learned friend, Mr. Weiner, concerning this statement that was provided to the Defence and presumably to the Court. Now, it's a difficult situation for the Defence in preparing for this trial and conducting it if we've been provided with suspect materials and materials that just don't reflect what the witnesses say. Of course that's not what the Defence position about this document is. But if you look on the final page of this document, you'll see that there is what's called an interpreter certification. And we would ask the Prosecutor now in good conscience and bearing in mind that they themselves have now launched an attack effectively on their own statement to call Peter Hewitt, the interpreter, to give evidence on this topic or to indicate whether or not the Prosecutors stand by the certification which was provided to the Defence and on which we and presumably the Court rely in preparing and running the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as I said, that that statement is not essentially important. It may be important in the cross-examination, but this statement will certainly not be admitted into the evidence. What we relied upon is the testimony of this witness in this courtroom. And at a later stage, if there's great disputes concerning of the translation, as we had with the document 108 for the last witness, we'll consult the CLSS or the interpreters on that very issue. But on this particular document, I don't see it's necessary to call the interpreters to testify to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, the reason why I raise it now rather than at a later time is because frankly the witness is here and I don't want to be accused of launching an attack after the witness has vanished. But what the witness says about the interpreting process is capable of impacting directly on his credit, on his credibility, and he is making grave allegations, really, and the Prosecutor are leading that evidence from him in redirect; quite grave, quite significant allegations are being made here. Now, if they're not true, that's another matter that you, the Tribunal, would be entitled the weigh up in considering whether you believe one word that he says. And for that reason, I want to mark that as an issue that the Defence raises, because these are grave allegations and if Peter Hewitt and the man who has been variously described as Mihajlovic and other things, but whose true name is Nikolai Mikhailov. Having engaged in tat sort of conduct, well, it could be a matter of significance one way, but of course if the answer is the other way, well, it affects this witness. So that's why I raise it now. I agree with Your Honour it's not a question o of the statement going into evidence, but it's a question of this witness's credibility and the way that he explains what's happened. I don't seek that any order be made about it right now, but I raise it now and the Prosecutor will have to consider what position they want to take about it, but I want to put it on the map because it's not going to go away, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, table

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- I believe that your observations or statement is in the record. And if in the future you believe there is a need for the further action, you may file a motion to that effect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Judge El Madhi. Questioned by the Court: JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, I wish to seek some verification in order to make sure that I understood you properly. It regards what happened on the 9th of September. You stated that you were together with the troops and that you heard yourself personally something that was said by Mr. Karic. Here's my question: Did you know this individual before you met him, before that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I did know him. And I can tell you again: Karic did say that, and I have to say again that I doubt very much that Mr. Halilovic and Zuka were able to hear it, because it wasn't shouted or said very loudly or anything. They were about 10 metres away from Karic when he said it. I can't say with any certainty, but I would be very surprised if they heard it, because they were quite a long way away and he wasn't shouting. He wasn't yelling. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. But you have no doubt as to him saying the sentence that you heard. It was Mr. Karic who said so? You're sure about this?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Did you know him -- had known him for a long time?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] How did you get to know him?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we had known each other from the beginning of the war. In fact, I didn't meet him at the beginning of the war. I just heard of him. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes. But how did you manage to identify him? Had you met him before, before the 9th September? I mean personally.

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would see him on and off from the outbreak of the war. I said this before. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] But then what was -- what were the clothes that he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in uniform. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Did he have any indication of rank?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Some indication that he belonged to the Supreme Command on the left arm, on the left side. I think they used to wear that sort of thing at the time. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And did he come across to you as being the highest ranking officer among the people present there?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you, witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge El Mahdi. Any questions out of Judge's questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Further examination by Mr. Weiner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you said that Mr. Karic did not appear to be the highest ranking officer there. Who was the highest ranking officer of those three?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about ranks. I don't think we had ranks at that time. I know that Karic was somewhere in the General Staff and -- and the -- somebody else was head of the General Staff, Chief of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the Chief of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Halilovic was Chief of the General Staff, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just one arising. But I make it clear that it's from what my friend asked and not what from Judge El Mahdi asked, but it would be one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let me see whether it's related to Judge El Mahdi's question or not. Further cross-examination by Mr. Morrissey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the question is going to be: Mr. Halilovic being Chief of the General Staff, was Rasim Delic the commander of the General Staff at that time?

utterances.speaker: NEDZAD MEHANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was. At any rate, Rasim Delic was commander of the army, and I'm not really sure about the hierarchy. I think Rasim Delic was army commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage, are there any documents to tender besides what we have already admitted into the evidence? Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, there are two. There's MFI176, which was a -- a list of the dates of persons enrolled in the 9th Brigade, or its predecessor, the 3rd Brigade. And there's MFI178, which is the -- the indictment which the Court will recall had on it the two names, Nedzad Mehanovic with all the relevant personal details of this witness, and also the future Prosecution witness who was at the top -- mentioned at the top of that indictment, subject to any measures he might seek. With respect to that last one, I'd submit that that should be tendered as an exhibit now because it's an official document even though the witness didn't agree that he'd actually viewed that document, it's plainly the official document upon which the proceedings against him commenced and he acknowledged speaking to a lawyer about it and he acknowledged that there was such an incident involving the three hand grenades. For that reason, I'd submit that that order be tendered through this witness. MFI176 has got a weaker basis for tendering. It seems uncontroversial to tender it but it's a matter whether the Prosecution will take an objection or not. This witness did not acknowledge seeing that document. So that has to be acknowledged at first. However, he acknowledged the information that was contained in it as being accurate. It is -- purports to be on its face anyway military information. I have to acknowledge that if the Prosecution took an objection to that, I think technically I would have to agree that it ought not to be tendered. But the Prosecution may choose not to object to it. I'm not sure. But it's -- I acknowledge he didn't see it. So those are the two documents I'm seeking to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any objections, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, number 176, it's a military document and we would not have an objection to a military document -- --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. This document MFI176 is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: With regard to document number 178, we do have an objection. The same basis as yesterday: Number one, this is not relevant to this matter; number two, this is just an indictment. There was no conviction. There's no certified copy of any conviction here. It's an irrelevant matter, and it should not be admitted. If at some future time they can tie the relevance of this to some evidence or to some issue in the case, then we would not have an objection. But at this time, it's not relevant and it should remain a -- a matter for identification at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Might I respond briefly to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, very -- very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- my friend's objections missed the target because it's not being put directly as the at credit of the witness in the sense of him being convicted. My learned friend says there's no certified copy here. I can assure this Court that there isn't going to be one and that he wasn't convicted, and I attempted to tender that, as you'll recall. So it's not being suggested that a Court has determined his guilt. The issue was the conjunction of the names on that document. And that's the reason why we submit -- so it's highly relevant, we say, but as to the other objection, it's a matter for the Court to deal with. But I submit that it's -- it is relevant from the point of view that I say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is not highly relevant. There's no question that this man served in three different units under the -- under Celo, who's Ramiz Delalic. His name -- he's testified about his -- his serving with Ramiz Delalic. There is no -- at this point, there is no relevancy to that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, after hearing the two parties and after consultation with my colleagues, we believe that the practice in this Tribunal is in favour of the admissibility as a rule and we also would like to mention that the mere admission of a document into the evidence does not in itself signify that the statements contained within should naturally be deemed as the true accurate portrayal of the facts. So long as this document is relevant and has some probative value as well as certain reliability, we believe that it could be admitted into the evidence. So the document 178 is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I've been reminded by Madam Court Deputy that this document should be admitted under seal. It is so decided. Well, witness, thank you very much for giving your evidence. Madam Usher will show you out of the room. You may go now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The two documents just admitted will be D176 and D178, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just indicate for the assistance of -- of the e-court procedures that both of those documents have been uploaded into the system as Your Honour instructed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have a few minutes left in this sitting. There's two matters I would like to mention. The first one is about the document MFI108. I would like to hear the positions from the Prosecution on this document, as I indicated before.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that document as well as the issue of protective measures for the witness following the next one are both matters that attorney Chana's -- is handling, and could those be considered after the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yeah, that's the second issue, that is, about your latest filings concerning of the protective measures. Maybe we should go into the private session and we'll hear the views from the Defence. Yes, we'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And the hearing is adjourned and we will resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Re, did you have a chance to talk to this witness about his rights? If not, would you please read Rule 90(E) to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If Your Honour can bear with me while I collect it from my folder on the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please. Examined by Mr. Re:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your name Enes Sakrak?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were born in 1973?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Not on the 19th but the 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I said May 1973. That was a -- it was misheard. Are you currently a prisoner in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His Honour the Presiding Judge has asked me to read to you Rule 90 of the Tribunal's Rules of Evidence and -- sorry, Procedure and Evidence, which is as follows: "A witness may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate the witness. The Chamber may, however, compel the witness to answer the question. Testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Re, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You've told -- just to clarify, you were born in May -- May 1973, and in September 1993 you would have been 20 years old; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In September 1993, were you a member of the 9th Motorised Brigade of the 1st Corps of the ABiH and stationed in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In October 2003, did you plead guilty at the Sarajevo Cantonal Court to the murder of Ljubica Zadro, then aged -- and her four-year-old daughter, Mladenka Zadro, the murder of them on the 9th of September, 1993 in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 4th of November, 2003, did the cantonal court in Sarajevo sentence you to a period of imprisonment of 10 years, from the 22nd of August, 2003?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you serving that sentence of imprisonment now?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sakrak, were you in fact guilty of those two murders? In other words, did you murder Ljubica Zadro and her four-year-old daughter, Mladenka Zadro on the 9th of September, 1993 in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, and I repent that act.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you first questioned by anyone about the murders of these two people in Grabovica in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date. I think it was The Hague investigators, but that doesn't mean the other soldiers were not questioned before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to a Hague investigator - Karl Konig, a lawyer - Nikolai Mikhailov in February 2000 in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that the first time that you had ever been questioned by anyone in authority about the murders?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, I personally was, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they questioned you, did you admit to the murders and tell the truth in that record of interview they conducted?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why was that?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know myself why, but nothing that I said at the time is true. I didn't wish to admit my guilt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you finally admit your guilt in late 2003?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Because I felt very bad about what I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back to -- sorry, going back to the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Were you a reserve police officer from April 1992 until about April 1993 in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then join the LARD-PVO? It's an acronym for the Light Artillery and Rocket Detachment of the Sarajevo Anti-Aircraft Defence?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that, did you join the 9th Motorised Brigade in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately when did you join the 9th?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: In early September, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know someone called Sead Karagic in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: A friend, an acquaintance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he also in the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know someone called Haris Rajkic?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: The same as Sead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Nihad Vlahovljak?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was he? Who was his role?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean when you say "what was his role."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew him. How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I knew him quite well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his position in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Company commander, the last one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in his company?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, the one that I belonged to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of your company?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: It didn't have a special name. I really couldn't recall the exact name of it right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In September 1993, did you know or know of a person called Ramiz Delalic, whose nickname was Celo?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: He was a good fighter, a great fighter. That's how I knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he also in the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his position within that unit?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was a commander or deputy commander of that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who Vahid Karavelic was?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: 1st Corps commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on the 7th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I think that we set off for Herzegovina then from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who's "we"?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: My brigade, the 9th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you receive your orders to set off for Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't understand. How we got the order? I don't -- I don't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was the order that you were to go transmitted to you as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: It was conveyed to us personally by the platoon commander. Actually, I don't know whether it was a company or a platoon exactly. I'm not very versed in these things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: In trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many soldiers went with you to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Approximately 60 or 70, according to my estimate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many trucks transported these soldiers to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Celo, Ramiz Delalic, accompany you to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you travel by day or night?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We left Sarajevo at night and we travelled that night and arrived in Herzegovina around noon the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you change trucks on the way at any point?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, at Bradina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you change -- what sort of -- what sort of transport did you change and take from there at that point?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Half were trucks and half buses. It was a little bit complicated, but that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many trucks and how many buses did you take from Bradina?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Also two, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By that last answer, do you mean that one was a truck and the other one was a bus?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: No. No. No. I think that woodcutters used that in Bosnia before. It was a truck that had been turned into a bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean a truck that looked like a bus?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were both vehicles trucks that looked like buses?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you stop in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: The first time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the morning -- you said you travelled overnight. Where did you stop in the morning in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: In Jablanica, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At about what time did you stop in Jablanica, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what time it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to dawn, was it daylight? And if so, how -- how long, doing your best, after daylight do you think it was?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: The best I can tell you is that it was around 10.00, 10.30 at most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where in Jablanica did you stop?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I think there was a unit, as I later heard from Mr. Zuka. I didn't know Zuka personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you referring to a military -- temporary military establishment known as Zuka's base, as the place where you stopped?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was temporary or not, but I think that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stop at Zuka's -- at this place for, Zuka's base?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Not long. I couldn't say exactly now. Maybe 15 to 20 minutes. Maybe half an hour. I wasn't paying attention to the time, so I couldn't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was discussed between the people who came with you and the people at Zuka's base when you got there?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We didn't come into contact at all. We didn't mingle. We didn't talk with Zuka's people. The only conversation there was was within the men of the 9th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to Zuka's base, did you see Celo, Ramiz Delalic? Did he get out of the truck buses?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he do?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: He went inside. I don't know who he talked to, but he was looking for accommodation for us, because the first thing for anyone to secure was food and accommodation and he was taking care of his men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he inform you, as the men, of the results of his inquiries of accommodation.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We were only told later that we were going to Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "later," do you mean before you set off for Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, after that conversation he had. When he came back, when Celo came back, we were told that we were going to Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Nihad Vlahovljak? Was he -- was he there at the time?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the existence of Grabovica before you were told you were going -- going there?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Only before the war, when I was going to the coast. There was a place you passed through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware on the day that you went there in 1993 of the ethnicity or nationality of the inhabitants of the village of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time -- I withdraw that. You said you arrived at midday before. Were you referring to arriving in Grabovica at midday, around midday?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember if Celo accompanied you to Grabovica on the 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: He did, but he returned immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Nihad Vlahovljak?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: He was with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you regard as the commander of the group of soldiers you travelled with to -- from Sarajevo to Jablanica and then Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Commander? You mean the whole brigade or just the platoon?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just the platoon that you -- or the soldiers you travelled with from Sarajevo to Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Out of the eight men that were with me, we regarded Nihad as platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any checkpoints between Jablanica and Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. There was a checkpoint at the destroyed bridge between Jablanica and Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it an ABiH checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I think it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where in Grabovica did your trucks that looked like buses stop?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: At the end of the road in Grabovica, outside a house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other soldiers there at the time that you arrived? I mean soldiers who were already there.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: The Solakovs [phoen] had already been put up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just clarify that last answer.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: What do you mean clarify? Solakov's unit or Solakovic's unit was already put up there. I don't know exactly the name of that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know it was them?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I knew a fellow from that unit. I knew that he was a member of that unit. And in addition, I believe it was said that those were Solakov's men

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Outside a house.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Solak's men. Solak seems to be the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: They were sitting around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier that Celo went back to Grabovica. What did he do -- sorry, went back to Jablanica. I apologise. What did he do before he went back to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We got out of the bus and then he told us that there were two empty houses that we should occupy, and then he returned to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "occupy," do you mean seek accommodation in, to sleep in for the night?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. We should stay there during the time that we spent there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go looking for these two empty houses?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. We all left and we went into those two empty houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "all," are you referring to the entire group of soldiers who came with you from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I mean the members of the 9th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And just to refresh my memory, did you say it was about 50 or 60 soldiers? Am I correct in that?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it possible -- I withdraw that. Were those houses big enough to accommodate all 50 or 60 soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Well, maybe yes, maybe not. They were not equal in size. One could take in more men than the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We went up, and since this place was not fit to accommodate us because it wasn't large enough, somebody - I don't know exactly who - passed the message to us, to our platoon, to go to the other house. But I underline here that nobody from my platoon just got up and went to the other house of their own accord.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean "passed a message"? Do you mean someone sent -- gave you an order or just suggested that you should do it?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the transcript, it says -- a moment ago: "Someone - I don't know exactly who - passed the message to us, to our platoon, to go to the other house." What I'm trying to clarify is your understanding. Do you mean that someone passed on an order to you or someone suggested something to you? Could I just ask you not to look -- not to look at --

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: It was more of an order than a suggestion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who conveyed the order to you? Mr. Sakrak, just stop. Can I just please ask you to close whatever you have in front of you there. Just put it -- put it to one side, please. Okay. The question is: Who conveyed the order to you, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Nihad was the one who told our platoon, my platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to Nihad, are you always referring to Nihad Vlahovljak?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you in fact go to the other houses looking for accommodation?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these other houses empty or inhabited?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: They were inhabited.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to a particular house yourself?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the people living or appearing to inhabit that house?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Two elderly people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how old were they?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: In my rough estimate, 70 to 80 years of age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they a couple?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I say "couple," I meant man and wife -- sorry, husband and wife.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn what their names were?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Pero and I believe the woman was Marica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn what their family name was?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. We had quite a normal conversation with the people, and the man told me their last name was Maric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was their reaction when you -- firstly - I withdraw that - how many of you went to Mr. Maric's -- Mr. And Mrs. Maric's place looking for accommodation?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Eight of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please give the Trial Chamber the names of the people who went with you to the Maric's house.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Nihad, Pedja, Klos, Hajre, Mesad, whom we also refer to as Musa, Rajkic, Karagic, and myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the reaction of Mr. And Mrs. Maric to the eight of you appearing at their house looking for accommodation?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: At first, they were taken aback. But after a brief discussion, they agreed to let us use two rooms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the eight of you in uniform?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you armed?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you armed with?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Side arms. In fact, an automatic rifle and 150 rounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the two -- sorry, did the eight of you divide yourselves amongst the two rooms?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it four each to a room?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Myself, Rajkic, and Karagic used one room; whereas, the rest took the other room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier you had quite a normal conversation with the people. How long did that last for, the quiet, normal conversation?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: For quite a while. It went on without any problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did problems occur?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I think it started when his son's photograph was found on which the son was wearing an HVO uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who found it?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you told what his son's name was?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't remember. I really don't remember whether it was mentioned or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the reaction of the soldiers to finding this photograph of the son wearing an HVO uniform? What did they do?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: All I know was that nobody hit him. Nobody did anything physical to him. There was verbal abuse, cursing, without physical violence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did this occur? Inside or outside the house?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Inside the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said "him" a Home -- moment ago, were you referring to the elderly -- Mr. Pero Maric?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of day or night was this approximately?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: 3.00, half past 3.00 maybe. But I can't say for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after the -- the verbal abuse and the cursing of Mr. Maric?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Nothing. Things calmed down and then we sat with him outside the house again and continued talking normally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the continuing talking normally last for this second time?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I really don't remember, but it was quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Then the man was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At about what time was the man killed? Was it light or dark?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Just before dark. It was already dusk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was the man - that's Pero Maric - when he was killed?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: He was sitting together with us at a table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is "us"? You mentioned eight people going to the house before. Was it those same eight or was it a different group of people?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: The same people mostly and some other people were coming and going, so the number and the composition of the group changed constantly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other people coming and going, were they soldiers from the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: For the most part. And I have to say I didn't know all the members of the 9th personally, so I wouldn't be able to say exactly that somebody was a member of the 9th Brigade or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Mustafa Hota?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in your unit?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: He was a member of the 9th, but he did not belong to my platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which platoon or company did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but it's the same brigade. I just don't know which platoon or company exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he one of these other soldiers who came to visit you when you were sitting talking to Mr. Maric at the table?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, he was sitting with us too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he do?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: He was sitting there talking, just as the rest of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he armed with?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, he also had an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he do with his rifle when he was at the table with you?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: What do you mean what he did?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was armed with a rifle. What did he do with it, when he had it with him at the table?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: After a while, he lifted the rifle and killed the man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that he shot Mr. Pero Maric?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just describe briefly to the Trial Chamber where the two of them were at the table in relation to each other. Were they on the said side, opposite sides?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: What do you mean "where they were"? Pero or Hota?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to each other.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: They were facing each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if anything, did Hota say when he shot Mr. Maric?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: That "Our charity will be our undoing."
