utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Because everybody treated us as doormats all the time. When I say "everybody," I mean all the other armies who passed through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "us," are you referring to your -- to your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: First of all, I have to say that I'm not a nationalist, but that's the way it looked like. That's the way it turned out all of the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Are you a Bosniak?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mustafa Hota, is he likewise a Bosniak?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when he made that comment, did you understand that he was referring to your position as Bosniaks in Bosnian society?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: The word "Merhamet" is very difficult to translate. When you say that, you mean a person who is -- who always gives in, who is charitable, who is nice to others. A lot of things are comprised in the word.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your reaction and the reaction of the soldiers with you to Hota shooting dead Mr. Maric in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: As for me, I was shocked. I suppose the others were too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone say anything to Hota to indicate displeasure at what he'd done?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Maric die immediately?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I think he did. Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to his body just at that point?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know whether we got up spontaneously or Nihad told us to get up. I think it was spontaneously that we got up and moved the body to the side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "the side," do you mean away from the table where you were sitting?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, did his body remain there for some time, that is, where you left it -- I'm sorry, where you moved it to?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, covered with a blanket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and the other soldiers you named before stay in Mr. Maric's house that night?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the other soldiers that you referred to coming and going? Did you see any other soldiers after Mr. Maric had been killed coming to the house?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: There were other soldiers, but I can't remember the names. That's one. And second, I didn't even know all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they aware or did they become aware, to your knowledge, that Mr. Maric had been murdered?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know whether they found out or not. I don't know what happened at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have -- hear any conversation indicating that other soldiers had some knowledge about the killing that night?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any commanders initiate an investigation, to your knowledge, into the murder of Mr. Maric on that night?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know. It's possible that nobody even knew what had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any military police or military security personnel or commanders come to the house looking to investigate the murder of this old man that night?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I didn't see anyone, which doesn't mean that nobody came while I was sleeping. I can't say with 100 per cent certainty that they either did or didn't come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was Mrs. Maric when her husband was being murdered?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Inside the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many shots did Hota fire, to your recollection, at Mr. Maric?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know. Not many shots. Two or three rounds. Not more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about shooting during the night? You said you heard him shoot Mr. Maric. Did you hear any other shooting during the night when you were staying in that house?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We heard shots when the woman was killed, but if you're going to ask me who killed her, I can't tell you. I can't tell you that either Hota or anybody else killed her for sure, because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you heard the shots that you understand killed Mrs. Maric?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I was in my room sleeping.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that during the night?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what time it was though. I was tired from the trip and we probably went to sleep early, but I don't know what time it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear any voices at the time that you heard the shots in the night?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: There were some voices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose voices were they?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know whose voices, but these two young men who were with me and I recognised only Hota's voice from the voices we knew from before. But that doesn't mean that Hota killed that woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the voices appear to be coming from? Inside or outside the house?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: From inside the house, I think. From the hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that Mrs. Maric was killed?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We saw that in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see her body?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was her body?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: In the bed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Her bed in her bedroom?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there blood?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I didn't notice that there was blood. Perhaps I wasn't paying attention to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know she was dead?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: She was lying and she wasn't moving. I didn't go up to her to touch her, but I could see that she wasn't moving. I didn't pay attention to the surroundings to see if there was any blood on the wall or anywhere, but I knew she was dead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the shooting you said you heard during the night, did you hear any other gunfire -- I'm sorry, the shooting -- and you heard the voice of Hota Mustafa, did you hear any other shooting during the night, that is, before dawn?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: When I woke up. Around the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About what time did you get up?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Perhaps at about 9.00 or 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go outside?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you go outside with?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: With Karagic and Rajkic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the shooting going on when you went outside?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Not so much. There was some shooting, but not very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was Nihad Vlahovljak when you went outside?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: In front of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to him?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. Not anything in particular, but just the usual. It wasn't any particular kind of talk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know someone called Habib Alic?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he around when you went outside?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I think that he was, but I'm not 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us earlier that Nihad was your company or platoon commander. What orders, if any, did he give you on the morning of the 9th of September; that's the morning after the killing of Mr. Maric.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: He conveyed the message to us. Knowing Nihad, I know that he wouldn't order something like that himself but that an order had come saying that the villagers were to be killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were your two colleagues -- comrades, Karagic and Rajkic, there with you when he told you that?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your response to his conveying that order to you? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We took our side arms and set off in the direction of the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to go back into the house to collect your side arms to do that?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other soldiers in the village when you set off in the direction of the village?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, perhaps they were there by the railway -- railroad. Perhaps one or two soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing members of Solakovic's unit when you were with your two colleagues going through the village?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I can't say whether they were members of Solak's or my brigade. There weren't any special markings or insignia. But I would like to emphasise that I didn't know everybody by name. I didn't know who belonged to which unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go into the village?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. I was already in the village, because the house where we were staying was in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We went along the railroad and then we turned left down some small path.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you turned left down some small path, did you have any conversations with other 9th Mountain Brigade -- sorry, Motorised Brigade soldiers who were in the village? Did you meet any and speak to them on the way?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We met some soldiers. I don't know whether they were from the 9th or not, but they said that everything was clear down there, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you understand them to mean to you when they said that everything was "clear down there"?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The soldiers said to you that everything was clear down there. Where were they referring to? What was down there?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: The village of Grabovica, also. It was actually the village of Grabovica. There is an upper part and a lower part, near the railroad and below the railroad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that you -- that Nihad conveyed an order to you that all the villagers were to be killed. Did you understand when they told you that the -- that everything down there was clear that it meant that the Croat villagers were no longer there, that they had been killed?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: You could say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of hearing that, did you not go to the village but go somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We didn't leave the village at any point. We just went along the road and then we branched off onto a small path on the left side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any -- the bodies of any civilians as you walked up to that path?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: A couple of people near the railway tracks, near the railroad station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You said "a couple." Can you be more specific as to numbers? Do you mean two or a greater number?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I wasn't paying attention. Perhaps two or three. Maybe more. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could Your Honour just excuse me for one moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sakrak, these two or three body, did you notice whether they were men or women or the ages of them, or children?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I didn't notice, but mostly they were elderly people. I don't know whether these were men or women. I'm not sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you turn left onto this path leading up the hill?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know why. Perhaps out of curiosity. No particular reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did you go up the hill with?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: With Karagic and Rajkic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was up the hill?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: A house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the leader of your small team of three?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was Karagic. I cannot state 100 per cent for sure that it was him. It was a small group. It was only the three of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other buildings were up the hill, apart from the house?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Next to the house -- I don't know. The house was on the right side. On the left side there was a -- a barn, a shed, and something like a summer kitchen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any people around this house and that barn and shed?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: They were sitting in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were there?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: An elderly couple, a younger couple, and three children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "couple," you meant a man and a woman?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old did they appear to be, the older couple?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: In their 70s or 80s. The younger couple was in -- they were in their 40s. And there were three children. I don't know the ages exactly, but that's more or less that age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The children, were they boys or girls?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Two boys and a girl.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the approximate age of the boys? Under 10? Over 10?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: About 10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the girl? Under five? Over five?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: She was younger. She was younger than they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she appear to be under five or over five?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak to them, this older and younger couple?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was said?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We were talking, and then we took the younger man towards the stable to give us the cow. Actually, we told him to come with us so we can take the cow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "we," do you mean the three of you?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the three of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us earlier that you were armed. What were you doing with your arms, that is, your weapons, when you went with the man towards the -- the stable?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: It was hanging. The weapons were hanging by -- at our side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go into the shed with him?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I went inside. The elderly couple also came with us. And since this younger man told them to come, I went inside with them -- actually, I went with him inside and the elderly pair remained outside with Karagic and Rajkic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you hear when you were inside the shed?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your reaction and the reaction of the younger man?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: The younger man started to shout and wail and he ran outside and I ran outside after him, and then I saw these two bodies lying there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose two bodies were they?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: The bodies of the elderly couple, the man and the woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they dead?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the shooting continue?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: When we went outside, then the two of them started to fire at the man who was beside me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close were you to this man?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Very close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you avoid getting shot yourself?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I stepped to the side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they hit him?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: He fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he likewise shot dead?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the three of you do then? Sorry, can I just -- I'll come to that in a moment. When they shot him, what was the distance between them and him? How close were they?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: It wasn't too far away. Perhaps maybe 2 or 3 metres at the most, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. After shooting the young man dead, where did the three of you go or what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We went back to the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was the younger woman, the mother?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: She wasn't in front of the house at that point in time. We looked for her when we were in the house, and I don't remember whether the two others found her or whether she came by herself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about her small daughter? Where was she?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: She was in her arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you take her?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Towards the barn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was she still carrying her child?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she have any jewellery or items of value on her or in the house?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I can't really remember. Maybe she had a ring on her finger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you or the other soldiers take the ring?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, I think that Rajkic asked for it and the woman gave the ring to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ask her for anything else, such as money or valuables?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I cannot remember those things at this very moment because I can't really remember all of those things any more, so I couldn't really tell you exactly. It's possible, but it's also possible that we didn't ask for anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take her into the barn with her young daughter?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We didn't. We just asked her to tie up the cow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did she do?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: She tied up the cow and handed it over to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that inside the barn?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: The cow was inside and she handed it over to us outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to her?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: With the woman?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and the girl.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: And then I killed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you do that?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: From the automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many shots did you fire at her?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was she still holding her child when you shot her?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you kill them both instantly?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what distance did you shoot this woman and her child?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We were not too far apart. There wasn't that much of a distance between us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you talking metres?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: A couple of metres, perhaps two or three metres apart. Not more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you do this? Why did you shoot dead this mother and the daughter?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I don't know why I did that. And I repent this act, and if I could, I would bring her back, the woman and the child, but I cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the other two say anything to you before you shot this woman and her child?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I really don't remember any longer whether any one of them told me to kill them or anything like that, but for me that's not important. What's more important for me is that I was the one who did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name -- or did you learn the name of this family of people who were murdered on that day?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I didn't know it then. I found out about it a long time after that. I know that their last name is Zadro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At about what time of day did these murders occur?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Perhaps from noon till about 1.00 or 1.30, but I'm not sure 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do with the five bodies?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: When I killed the woman and the child, I turned around and then we dropped down immediately. I didn't really pay attention to anything. This is not something that is easy to do. I couldn't bear to watch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean "we dropped down immediately"? Are you saying to the ground or are you saying that you left the area?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: What I am saying is that we went back along the same path that we came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Leaving the bodies there?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you kill the two young boys as well?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they were when you -- or what happened to them when the three of you were killing the rest of the family?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I didn't see them after that. Which doesn't mean that any of the three of us would have actually killed any of those two boys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the four adults you killed were all civilians, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: You could say that. Although, it's not ruled out that the person who was in their 40s, the man who was in his 40s, was not a member of some military or some army. He could have been, but maybe he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, he wasn't -- sorry, I withdraw that. Was he wearing a uniform or armed when you shot him -- I'm sorry, when your -- your colleague shot him?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: He wasn't wearing a uniform, but many people in Bosnia didn't have uniforms but they were not civilians. They were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He didn't have a weapon, did he, when he was shot? He wasn't armed?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go when you went back down the hill, the three of you?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I think we went back towards the house, crossing the railroad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other bodies, apart from the two or three you saw near the railway earlier, when you went back into the village?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us earlier that Nihad conveyed the order that the Croats -- or the -- sorry, the villagers had to be killed. Having gone and killed some Croats in the village, did you go back and tell him what you'd done?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I think that we did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what you said to him?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I can't recall the exact words right now, but something to the effect that, "We killed them," to put it mildly. I don't want to complicate things by trying to say exactly what it was that we said, which words we used, but the gist of it was that we had killed them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other soldiers, apart from the three of you, there when you told him this?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I think that there were, but I'm not absolutely sure. These things do not remain in my memory, other than the things that I described, the things that I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when you reported back to Nihad about what you'd done?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I cannot say that it was a report. We just told him. A report is something else. We were in front of the house, and it was just conveyed that it was what we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're referring to the house you stayed in? That's Mr. Maric's house?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his reaction and the reaction of any other soldiers who were there when you told him of what you'd just done?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What time do Your Honours want to take the -- the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How long are you going to be for your direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Maybe another 15, 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid we have to take a break, and we'll resume at ten minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before the break, Mr. Sakrak, you were telling us about when you told Nihad what you had done. Just to clarify something from earlier, you told the Trial Chamber earlier that he had given you or conveyed an order to you that all the Croat villagers were to be killed and that the order came from someone higher up. Did he ever tell -- did he tell you at the time who the order came from or who gave him the order?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: He didn't tell me about the order for killing, but he told me who gave the order to bury the bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who gave -- who gave the order to bury the bodies?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Vehbija Karic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was Vehbija Karic, to your understanding?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: A high rank. A high rank in the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which corps or unit or group or command do you understand that he was of a high rank?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to go back also briefly to something from your earlier testimony. You told the Trial Chamber about Mustafa Hota. Which unit was he a member of, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: The 9th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which sub-unit, company, or platoon he was a member of?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you earlier about a person called Habib Alic, who was also a soldier from the 9th Motorised Brigade, who you said you saw on the 9th of September. That's day that the Zadro family was killed. Where did you see him that day?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Outside the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the house you were staying in, Pero Maric's house?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he tell you about what he had been doing that day?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: That he had killed a woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did he tell her and in what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Inside a house. But under what circumstances, I don't know. In fact, I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he tell you about how and why he'd killed her?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Allegedly he tried to rape her and then he killed her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it by shooting?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Probably. He didn't go into detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I showed you a photograph, would you be able to point out to the Trial Chamber which house it was he told you he had killed her in?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I hope so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to that a little bit later. Now, you said you saw Celo on the 8th of September and he went to Jablanica. Did you see Celo again - that's Ramiz Delalic - in Grabovica between when he went to Jablanica and when Nihad gave you the order to kill all the villagers?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you next see Celo?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: When the two boys were found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were the two -- are they the two boys who were the brothers of the little girl who you -- you shot?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they the same two boys that you saw at the Zadro family's house, up on the hill.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you hear that Celo had found the two boys?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know when exactly I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you come to hear about it?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know. Somebody said that two boys had been found and that Celo was beside himself with anger that something like that had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your reaction? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: It was my personal reaction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What did you do when you found out that -- that Celo was beside himself with anger about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: He stayed inside the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said, "He stayed."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: I stayed inside the house. The witness is not very easy to understand.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I. I, not he.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the two men you were with who also shot members of the Zadro family? Where were they when -- I withdraw that. Were you -- did you stay in the house with them?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that a line-up was being conducted of some soldiers in the village?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you stay inside the house?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Because if the boys had identified us, then Celo would have probably meted out an appropriate sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you think he would have done to you?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: He would have probably turned us over to the military police and charges would have been pressed against us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any line-ups, apart from that one that you didn't go in, did you ever go in any line-ups in Grabovica when you were there?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Just before we left for Dreznica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a line-up to select soldiers to go to Dreznica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A little earlier you told the Trial Chamber that there was an order to hide the bodies. When were you given that order?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly the date, but it could have been the 9th that the order arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was the order conveyed to you? Who told you?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Nihad passed it on to us, and as I said earlier, the order came from Vehbija Karic to bury those bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doing your best, can you try as hard as you can to tell the Trial Chamber what Nihad said or words to the effect of.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Well, if I can put it this way: He said that an UNPROFOR check was coming and that the bodies need to be buried.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did he tell this to?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know to whom exactly he said this, but it was conveyed. It was passed on to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe my question was unclear. I -- I'm referring to Nihad, not Karic. Did Nihad personally tell you and other soldiers that the bodies needed to be buried?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of that, did you and the other soldiers look for bodies to bury?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I only took part in the burial of the bodies of Pero and his wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were their bodies still respectively in the bed, that's Mrs. Maric, and outside, near the table, that's Mr. Maric?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I think both bodies were lying covered outside the house. I believe the woman's body had been carried out by that time. Either it was just before the burial or earlier. I'm -- I can't remember any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you bury them?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: A place overlooking the house, near the shed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the ground?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, in the ground. Nobody mutilated the bodies, as some stories would have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who helped you bury these two bodies?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: What do you mean who helped us? Who helped me personally or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I meant you, singular.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I can't remember those people, but they were all from the group that were staying in the same house with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you referring to soldiers from the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, I mean the members of my company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who disposed of or buried the bodies of the five members of the Zadro family that were murdered on the 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the bodies of the civilians, the two or three civilians lying near the railway that you saw on your way up to the Zadros' house? Do you know where -- where or how they were buried?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know, but I suppose they too were buried in the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Croat villagers remaining in that -- in the village of Grabovica by the night of the 9th of September, 1993? That's the day that the Zadro family was murdered.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe I did not understand your question very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you know, were there any Croat villagers left in Grabovica by the 9th -- by the night of the 9th?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you see any live Croat villagers after you returned from the killing of the Zadro family? Were there any Croat villagers still alive in that village that you saw?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I didn't see anyone, which doesn't mean that there were no live Croats left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you as a soldier before you went to Grabovica ever receive any training on the treatment of civilians or prisoners of war and the treatment of them?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I did not, but I suppose I should have received such training while I was on the police force, so I can't really blame the army for not training me, because I joined the army only in 1993 sometime after the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any training on the Geneva Conventions and their applicability in warfare?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see anything -- did you see anything in Grabovica after the Croat villagers were murdered on the 8th and 9th of September that indicated to you that there was an investigation into their deaths?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I can't say there was no investigation, because after that I left for Dreznica, so it's possible that there was an investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days did you remain in Grabovica after you participated in killing members of the Zadro family?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Not many days, but I can't tell you exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two, three, four? One?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Maybe two. Maybe three days. Certainly not more. Possibly less. I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that period, are you telling the Trial Chamber nothing occurred in the village to suggest that there was an active investigation into those murders of Croat villagers?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I can't say that there was no active investigation, that there were no inquiries made at all. I just know that I wasn't asked any questions, which doesn't mean that other soldiers were not questioned. I can't say one way or another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier that an order was conveyed to bury the bodies because UNPROFOR wanted to come to the village or was -- or something to that effect. In those -- in those days you remained in Grabovica after the killings, did you see any UNPROFOR soldiers coming to the village?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about members of the foreign press?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there --

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any physical impediment to UNPROFOR entering the village of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know. Unless you mean that checkpoint, but that checkpoint would have been unable to stop the UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Were you aware of the -- at the time of the name of the combat operation in Herzegovina that you and your fellow soldiers from the 9th were sent to participate in?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I wasn't aware, because the name itself did not mean anything to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of who -- what had you been told about what sort of operation it was?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We were told that we were supposed to go and help out the men in Herzegovina, the troops in Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear, if anything, about who was in charge of this operation?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Our assumption was that it was Mr. Sefer, which does not necessarily mean that he was, because nobody told us in so many words that it was him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "Mr. Sefer," do you mean Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I mean General Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about refugees? Were there refugees in Grabovica when you were there?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. They were on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they civilians?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any of them participate in the killing of the Croatian villagers?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: No. Those people were starving. They occasionally came to us to look for some food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I wish to show you some photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness -- can we please broadcast Exhibit P7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the photograph on the screen in front of you, Exhibit P7?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are three houses in this photograph. Were any of these the houses that you stayed in? Oh, sorry, firstly, do you recognise this as a photograph of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, this first house, the largest one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The largest one? Are you referring to the one at the bottom left of the photograph? The white one with a roof?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was staying in that house?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Solak's men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the house above it? Were any 9th Brigade soldiers staying in that?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Possibly, but I can't say with 100 per cent certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the house to the right, the white one without a roof? Was that a house occupied by the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In that area shown on the photograph, can you see a place where the trucks -- or trucks that looked like buses stopped, when you arrived in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: This track or road down there lined with trees. You see those trees there is, towards the bottom -- or rather, not trees but logs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Near the logs which are in the bottom right-hand side of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Could Exhibit P3 please be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just have a look at this one. This is -- when it comes onto the screen. Now, this is a -- do you recognise this as a -- a wider picture of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I want you to do on this, if you can get the pen which the court officer will provide you with, I want you -- can you see on that the house where you stayed? That's Mr. And Mrs. Maric's house.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I can't see it here, but I can tell you approximately where it was. Because it's not visible in this picture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Would you be able to mark a -- put a circle over where it is and just put a "1" in that.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You also referred earlier to Mr. Habib Alic going to a house and killing a woman. Can you see the house in which he said he killed the woman on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Here approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you put a "2" in the middle of that, please.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No objection. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. It's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Prosecution Exhibit P179.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just for the purposes of identification of that house on a different photograph, can the witness please be shown Exhibit P78.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you see clearly that photograph? It's got some numbers and markings on it. Just look at the arrows. I just want you to identify -- no?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want you to identify from those arrows with numbers on the top which was the house in which you were staying.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I think it's number 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness now please -- can we please now broadcast P86.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want you to mark two things on this. Can you see on that photograph the Zadros' house? Can you please just circle that and put a "1" outside the circle, because I think it's a very small house.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I think that's here. I don't know exactly where, but it's somewhere around here. Possibly here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible to enlarge that portion of the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's -- we can lose the circle. It doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that clearer?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you please just put a -- a "1" above that. Not inside. Above.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is it possible to move the screen to the side without -- without changing the dimensions? Just move it along. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry to take so much time on this. I'll have to ask you to mark again -- do you think you'll be able to recognise from where you marked that on the large one, if you could do the same -- don't do it now. If you could reduce it -- I want you to mark two things on the map.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if we now reduce it, could you mark two things on the map? You'll lose that circle. All right. I want you to mark two things on the map: Firstly, where you were when Nihad gave you the order to kill all the civilians; and, secondly, where the Zadro house is. A "1" and a "2".

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Nihad did not issue the order. He just transferred it or conveyed it to us. And that was here. That was the house where Zadro was. This is number 1 and this is number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. May that be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This photograph will be Prosecution Exhibit P180.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could we please broadcast Exhibit P22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sakrak, do you recognise what's in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: The Zadro family house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-examination -- any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Mettraux:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Sakrak. My name is Guenael Mettraux and I'm appearing on behalf of Sefer Halilovic. You've indicated during your examination-in-chief that you met a number of times with the Prosecutor investigator; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also met in late December 2004 with a representative of the Defence, investigator Medina Delalic, and myself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to a court order issued by this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Sakrak, you fully cooperated with the Defence and were truthful if your responses to our questions, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I hope so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to take you back a few years, at the start of the war in 1992; more precisely, at the time you were just fresh out of high school. You were 19 also; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were considering going to university after your high school.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Which is quite natural.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But instead of going to university, the war caught up with you and you had to choose another career, so to say; you had to enrol in the army. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it wasn't really a -- a choice for you, Mr. Sakrak. It was more of a duty or a necessity, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, Sarajevo was encircled.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, in a tight circle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was shelled every day, shelled at?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And no one really inside the city was ready for what was going on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. It's quite natural.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had no military experience, Mr. Sakrak. You had not done your compulsory military service at the time.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had no -- I'm sorry. And you had no inclination either for a military career.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You joined because you had to.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, sir, the Bosnian --

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I apologise. It was more of a duty for the defence, our own defence, the family, the city. It wasn't a question of necessity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was a matter of survival for your people, Mr. Sakrak, wasn't it that, that all able-bodied Bosniaks or Bosnians of other ethnicities --

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- would serve in the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Regardless of their ethnicity. Whoever felt as a Bosnian joined the B and H army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time, sir, you didn't have much weapons to fight against the shelling that was landing every day in Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you had is your courage and the courage of those who had enrolled in the army.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And life was rather hard at the time in Sarajevo, sir, for you as a soldier but also for civilians.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Exceptionally hard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Food was rare and life was dangerous, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object. Is this going to be tied to the substance of the witness's examination-in-chief at any point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, in the cross-examination, you know, the questions is not necessary to be tied to the direct examination, so I think that objection is overruled. But, however, it should be relevant. Maybe the question is too extensive, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, it is, Your Honour, if I may, relevant to a number of issues. That -- the evidence we've heard is far is very sanitised, if I may say so, version of the events and we think it is relevant to a full understanding of those events to know what the situation was at the time and under what condition the unit which we are talking about were operating, and it may become very relevant to the issue of membership to a particular unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, I didn't see that. I hope you could escape this part of question and come to which is really relevant as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will move on then, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated earlier to the Prosecution that you have received no training in the Geneva Conventions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You neither received any training in relevant humanitarian law treaties, had you.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you understood very well, Mr. Sakrak, at the time that the killing of civilians would be legal [sic], regardless of the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: You would assume that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And even furthermore, you would understand that this would be regarded as a criminal act.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't need a reminder of that, sir. You knew it before you left for Herzegovina, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't wish to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But I think my learned friend actually said "legal," and it was picked up in the transcript, so I don't think it would be picked up in the correction. He said, "You would assume that these killings of civilians would be legal." I heard him say "legal." It may have been interpreted as "illegal," but the answer seems to be directed to "illegal." So maybe we could clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, maybe could --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Absolutely, I'm grateful to the Prosecution for that remark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you the question again, Mr. Sakrak, if I may: You understood at the time the killing of civilians regardless of the circumstances would be regarded as illegal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also realised, as I asked you before, that this would constitute a criminal act.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I pointed out or proposed to you earlier, you didn't need a reminder of that fact; you knew it.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a few questions in relation which were also asked during your examination about the timing at which you became a member of the 9th Brigade. You've indicated, if I'm correct, that you joined in early September 1993. Could it have been a few days -- three or four days prior to going to Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: It's possible. It's quite possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you only formally became a member later on, sometime in November 1993? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the exact date of your formally becoming a member of the 9th Brigade was the 30th of November, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact date, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, could I ask that the witness be shown what is D965, DD00.2691. It is an excerpt of the log -- of the logbook, I'm sorry, of the 9th Motorised Brigade of the 1st Corps. Could the court staff please turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Sakrak, can you see the excerpt of that log in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read out the third name on the list with the number "222" in the first left column.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: The last and the first name?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Enes Sakrak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the date of birth in the next column on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read the date?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: 13th of May, 1973 in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, is that your date and place of birth, Mr. Sakrak?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I may ask the court staff to move on a bit to the right and perhaps a bit up so that the title of the document can be seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see the subtitle, Mr. Sakrak, called -- or named "Date of enrolment"?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: The 30th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it appears in the column marked "Date of enrolment"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's the date, Mr. Sakrak, at which you formally joined in the 9th Brigade, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well. I would like to offer this document at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: MFI181, I would believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any English translations of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, it should be uploaded on the system, Your Honour. It is uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution just has a question about the provenance of this document, which appears to refer throughout to the JNA. We weren't aware that the witness was alleged to be a member of the -- the JNA or the JNA was participating in this particular armed conflict. Perhaps if that could clarify -- be clarified and some evidence be given as to the provenance of this document; its source, and its chain of custody, the Prosecution would be in a much better position to indicate its position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, as far as the chain of custody is concerned, this document has been obtained from the archives of the army. As far as the reference to the JNA at the top is concerned, it would appear that the Bosnian army continued to use calendars or documents which were used by the previous army. If Mr. Re needs any further information as to the chain of custody of that document, we would be able to provide it perhaps not today but certainly in the -- at a later stage, perhaps tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution position is that the Defence is -- is seeking chain of custody on every single -- or basically every military document that we've produced. Now, if the Defence wishes to produce documents which purport to come from another army altogether, the Prosecution likewise asks them to produce proper evidence to be tendered to the Trial Chamber as to the source of these documents. It can't be okay for one party to stand up in court and say, "Oh, these are from the archive and this is what 'JNA' means," but the other party has to produce evidence as to the source of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you have any more information to tell us, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Not at this stage, I would be happy to provide that information. But considering that Mr. Sakrak has given us the evidence which we asked from him, I don't intend to pursue the matter. But in relation to the more fundamental question of the source of document and if required we will definitely provide that information to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll hold the admission of this document to a later stage. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sakrak, you were not the only member of the 9th Brigade that went to Herzegovina to have joined recently; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: It's possible. I don't know for sure, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Sead Karagic, for instance, had joined very recently, hadn't he?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you indicated, I believe, that you had joined that brigade precisely because you had friends and acquaintances within that brigade; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were you enrolled in the 9th Motorised Brigade, Mr. Sakrak, you had no reason to think that criminals were members of that brigade nor had you heard any rumours to that effect, had you?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I agree with you entirely, and I would like to take this opportunity to say that the 9th Mountain -- Motorised was not considered to be a criminal unit, like it's being said. Everybody had respect for that unit. Its fighters were good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was in fact regarded as an elite unit, sir; isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: You can say that, yes, if -- you can use that word, "elite."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it had taken a fundamental part in the defence of Sarajevo; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by the summer of 1993, the section of front line defended by the 9th Brigade in or around Stari Grad was one of the best defended in the city; isn't that so, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the 9th Brigade had also performed extremely well in other offensive and dangerous operations, like on Mount Igman; isn't that so, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, is this by reputation or is this something the witness heard or something the witness saw? Did he participate in it? Is it the reputation of the 9th in Sarajevo? Where is it going to? It's just got to be put -- it's just got to be put more precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But I believe that piece of evidence is relevant to this case and -- Maybe you could ask a specific question on that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think the question was sufficiently specific, Your Honour. I'll move on to another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No. My objection remains, and that is if my learned friend is asking the witness questions about the reputation of the brigade - and that is an issue in this case, and of course he's entitled to ask those questions - the evidence has to be precise. It has to be based upon the witness's knowledge. Is it his personal knowledge? Is it something that he heard, something that he saw for himself? How does he know? Did he read it in the newspaper, see it on the television, whatever?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you have a problem on that issue, you have the full opportunity to challenge that piece of the information during your redirect examination. You may proceed, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be clear on that point, Mr. Sakrak, you personally had not heard stories of this 9th Brigade being a criminal one. I'll be more precise perhaps to make the point. You didn't see any crimes being committed by any members of the 9th Brigade before this incident obviously?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I will tell you one thing regarding the 9th Brigade. That unit was not a criminal unit as it's being described. It had very good fighters. It numbered about a couple of thousand people. And the town was proud of it and it was a matter of pride to belong to such a unit precisely because it comprised good fighters and not criminals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was also a matter of pride for the city for another reason, sir, which is that it was a multi-ethnic unit or brigade, I should say; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were members of the Serbian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Members of the Croatian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And obviously members of the Bosniak ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. Nobody paid attention who was what in that unit. They were judged according to their fighting skill. They were no criminals. I get very upset when the 9th Brigade is described as a -- a criminal brigade. I get very upset because this simply just wasn't true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that we have the right picture in our mind about the size of the brigade, I think you mentioned its size -- was it somewhere between four and five thousand members at the relevant time, in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible. I don't know the exact number, but the brigade had a large number of soldiers. It covered a wide area, and that's why it numbered so many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would -- it would have been in that sort of figure, sir, in the thousands, four or five thousand members?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to move on now, sir, if I may to something different; namely, your being sent to Herzegovina. Despite the fact that you had just become a -- a member, although not formally yet a member of the 9th Brigade, you were immediately sent within days to Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you, sir, were selected personally by Nihad Vlahovljak to go to Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The selection for the individual members who went there was done at the brigade level and, in your case, more precisely at the platoon level; isn't that so, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sead Karagic and Haris Rajkic were also picked and selected by Nihad; isn't that the case, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you indicated to the Prosecutor today that the order to go to Herzegovina was given by your, and I quote, "platoon commander." That platoon commander, sir, that was Nihad, Nihad Vlahovljak?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Conveyed, conveyed the order, because to issue and to convey are two different things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the only thing that you know for sure is that as far as you're concerned, the order came from Nihad. Is that your evidence, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you travelled with your friends and colleagues at the time, you had no reason, sir, to believe that something terrible would happen in Herzegovina and certainly not something that eventually happened; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We didn't -- we didn't know anything. No mention had been made of any such possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you, Mr. Sakrak, had no intention to hurt anyone or to hurt any civilian, to be more precise?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Of course I didn't have any such intention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All you were thinking about as you were driving with your colleagues was the forthcoming fighting.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated earlier that Nihad was -- or was regarded, I should say, as platoon commander; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at the time, sir, he had no official rank and no official position within the brigade or the platoon.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't understand. He had no visible mark of any rank, no visible insignia of -- of ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And he had no official position, no official rank. He was just known or regarded by you as being the platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Something like that. I don't know whether he held a rank officially, but he didn't have anything on his uniform to distinguish him as a commander of platoon or anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
