utterances.text: I'm not asking you to make any -- any guesses, Mr. Sakrak, so that it's clear between us. Within that platoon which was headed, so to say, by Nihad, were the mere foot soldiers, if I may call them that, like yourself?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were people who made the link between you, the foot soldiers, and Nihad; isn't that the case, sir?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your case, that person was Sead or Sejo Karagic.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Remaining within this brigade, then, the individuals who were sent to Herzegovina, sir, do you know a man by the nickname Zuti?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't hear that nickname down in Grabovica in September 1993 as you were there, did you?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. As you arrived in the village, you've indicated that another unit had preceded you in that village and that unit, sir, was the Solakovic unit.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The official name of that unit was the 2nd Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: That's possible, but we always called them Solak's men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's okay.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: We never referred to them by any other name, so it's possible that this 2nd Independent Battalion was in fact what we knew as Solak's men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And that unit, sir, was, just like the 9th Motorised Brigade, a 1st Corps unit or, in your case, brigade.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was normally based in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And aside from the 9th Motorised Brigade and the 2nd Independent Battalion, that was the only so-called Sarajevo unit present in Grabovica at the time.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other so-called local units in Grabovica at the time? And I'm referring to the Handzar Division and the Cedo's Wolves.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you now a few questions about your accommodation as you arrived in the village of Grabovica. You've indicated that Ramiz Delalic, Celo, told the soldiers to go and accommodate themselves in two empty houses; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to point at those two houses if shown a picture?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: I should hope so. I just hope it's going to be a larger photograph, because on one side of the road there was a small hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could we see the Prosecution Exhibit 3 -- P3. P3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see the picture of Grabovica on your screen, Mr. Sakrak?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be able from this picture to identify the two houses in question?

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark them perhaps, with the assistance of the court usher.

utterances.speaker: ENES SAKRAK
utterances.text: That's here. The two houses, the two empty houses, were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sakrak.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could we offer this picture in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be document D182.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Mr. Mettraux, I think it's time. And there's two things I would like to remind both parties: The first one is tomorrow we are going to sit in the morning, 9.00 in the same courtroom, instead of the afternoon, since tomorrow is the Friday. The next issue is a request to the Defence team: Try to dig up some chain of custody of that document tonight. Maybe when we come to the admission of the evidence at a later stage we need your explanations. Well, witness, I'm afraid that you have to stay here for another night at least, so I have to remind you that you are under the oath, so do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony today. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The hearing for today is adjourned.
